sights.n: Uezu House, Kume Island (上江洲家住宅)
sights.address: 816 Nishime, Kumejima-chō, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: Ryūkyū-kingdom samurai residence of the Uezu family, district heads descended from the lords of Gushikawa Castle, built around 1754: red-tiled main house, hinpun screen wall and well inside limestone walls and fukugi windbreaks. A national Important Cultural Property.

sights.n: Tuyumya-baka — Tomb of Nakasone Tuyumya, Miyako (仲宗根豊見親の墓)
sights.address: 3-4 Nishi-Nakasone Makago, Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: Stone tomb built in the late 15th century by Nakasone Tuyumya, the chieftain who unified Miyako, for his father; it fuses Miyako's 'myāka' great-stone tomb with the main island's chamber-tomb style. The Tuyumya tombs are a national Important Cultural Property.

sights.address: Northern tip of Zamami Island, Zamami-son, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: Hilltop lookout on Zamami's north side, about an hour's walk from the port; on clear days Aguni, Tonaki and Kume islands are visible, and it is the best spot for watching humpback whales, which frequent these waters December–April. Part of Keramashotō National Park.

sights.n: Kaminohama Observatory, Zamami (神の浜展望台)
sights.address: West Zamami Island (30 min walk west of Ama Beach), Zamami-son, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: West-facing lookout on Zamami over Aka, Geruma and the scattered Kerama islets — one of the island's sunset viewpoints, a 30-minute walk from Ama Beach.

sights.n: Nishibama Beach, Aka Island (ニシバマビーチ)
sights.address: North-east Aka Island, Zamami-son, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: Aka-jima's signature beach: a long straight run of white sand shelving into gradations of 'Kerama Blue', within Keramashotō National Park.

The first war memorial raised after the Battle of Okinawa, built by residents themselves in February 1946 from gathered remains; enshrining some 35,000 people, it is the largest in the prefecture, and families gather here at dawn every Irei-no-hi (23 June).
